title: YEARS Algorithm for PE
sources: van der Hulle T et al. Lancet 2017 (YEARS study); van der Pol LM et al. NEJM 2019 (Pregnancy-Adapted YEARS)
purpose: A simplified diagnostic pathway that uses a variable D-dimer threshold to safely reduce CT pulmonary angiography. Count the three YEARS items, then apply the D-dimer cutoff: 0 items → cutoff 1000 ng/mL; ≥ 1 item → cutoff 500 ng/mL.

items.label: Clinical signs of DVT (unilateral leg swelling / pain on palpation)
PE is the most likely diagnosis (clinical gestalt — is PE at least as likely as any alternative?)

interpretation.label: Zero YEARS items → use D-dimer cutoff 1000 ng/mL. D-dimer < 1000 → PE excluded, NO CT. D-dimer ≥ 1000 → CT pulmonary angiography
≥ 1 YEARS item → use D-dimer cutoff 500 ng/mL. D-dimer < 500 → PE excluded, NO CT. D-dimer ≥ 500 → CT pulmonary angiography

notes: YEARS was validated without age-adjustment — do not stack age-adjusted D-dimer on top. Pregnancy-Adapted YEARS adds: if clinical signs of DVT, do compression ultrasound first (a positive US confirms VTE and stops the workup). Overall YEARS cut CTPA use by ~14% vs. Wells + fixed D-dimer with a 3-month VTE failure rate of 0.43%. Do not use in haemodynamic instability (that patient goes straight to imaging / bedside echo).
buildNote: Algorithm — item count selects the D-dimer threshold, it is not a summed risk score.
